## windows — 42 actions not declared

- [ ] `sg_actions.lookup`: macOS only: Look Up opens the system dictionary panel on the word under the pointer. Windows and Linux have no system dictionary panel.
- [ ] `sg_actions.system_app_switcher`: macOS only: macOS switches between applications, each holding its windows. Windows and Linux switch between windows with Alt+Tab: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `app_switcher`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.app_previous`: macOS only: macOS switches between applications, each holding its windows. Windows and Linux switch between windows with Alt+Tab: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `app_switcher`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.app_previous_screen`: macOS only: macOS switches between applications, each holding its windows. Windows and Linux switch between windows with Alt+Tab: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `app_switcher`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.space_prev`: Spaces on macOS and desktops on Windows and Linux are the same virtual desktops under two names: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `desktop_prev`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.space_next`: Spaces on macOS and desktops on Windows and Linux are the same virtual desktops under two names: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `desktop_next`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.space_prev_wrap`: Spaces on macOS and desktops on Windows and Linux are the same virtual desktops under two names: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `desktop_prev_wrap`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.space_next_wrap`: Spaces on macOS and desktops on Windows and Linux are the same virtual desktops under two names: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `desktop_next_wrap`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.mission_control`: Each system has its own window overview: Mission Control and App Exposé on macOS, Task View on Windows. Linux desktops each bind their own, so bind your desktop's key as a keystroke there. Equivalent actions: `task_view`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.app_expose`: Each system has its own window overview: Mission Control and App Exposé on macOS, Task View on Windows. Linux desktops each bind their own, so bind your desktop's key as a keystroke there. Equivalent actions: `task_view`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.run_apple_shortcut`: macOS only: Apple Shortcuts exist only on macOS. Elsewhere, run a command or a program instead. Equivalent actions: `run_program`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.clear_notifications`: This system lets no application dismiss notifications: clear them in the notification centre, which the equivalent action opens. Equivalent actions: `notification_center`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.remove_quarantine_selection`: Each system marks downloaded files its own way (the quarantine attribute on macOS, the Mark of the Web on Windows) and offers the action that removes its own mark. Linux marks no downloaded file. Equivalent actions: `unblock_file_selection`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.make_executable_selection`: Not on Windows: a file runs there because of its extension, not because of an executable permission.
- [ ] `sg_actions.layer_on`: macOS only: these switch the navigation layer kept inside Karabiner-Elements. On Windows and Linux the layer follows the key held down and has no switch to set.
- [ ] `sg_actions.layer_off`: macOS only: these switch the navigation layer kept inside Karabiner-Elements. On Windows and Linux the layer follows the key held down and has no switch to set.
- [ ] `sg_actions.capsword`: This system offers the same action under another name: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `caps_word`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.save`: Not a separate action on this system: it is one of its modifier + key combinations (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl on Windows and Linux), listed under “Shortcuts”.
- [ ] `sg_actions.opt_backspace`: Each system deletes a word with its own modifier (Option on macOS, Ctrl on Windows and Linux), so each lists its own action: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `ctrl_backspace`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.opt_delete_fwd`: Each system deletes a word with its own modifier (Option on macOS, Ctrl on Windows and Linux), so each lists its own action: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `ctrl_delete`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.cmd_backspace`: macOS only: Cmd+Delete deletes to the start or the end of the line in macOS text fields. Windows and Linux text fields have no such key: select to the line edge with Shift+Home or Shift+End, then delete.
- [ ] `sg_actions.cmd_delete_fwd`: macOS only: Cmd+Delete deletes to the start or the end of the line in macOS text fields. Windows and Linux text fields have no such key: select to the line edge with Shift+Home or Shift+End, then delete.
- [ ] `sg_actions.cmd_shift_tab`: macOS only: macOS switches between applications, each holding its windows. Windows and Linux switch between windows with Alt+Tab: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `app_switcher`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.spotlight`: macOS only: this action opens Spotlight, the search of macOS. On Windows or Linux, bind your desktop's own search shortcut as a keystroke instead.
- [ ] `sg_actions.sticky_shift`: This system offers the same action under another name: use the equivalent action. Equivalent actions: `one_shot_shift`.
- [ ] `sg_actions.open_console`: Each driver debugs through its own runtime: AutoHotkey provides Window Spy, a variable listing and a key history, and Hammerspoon provides a Lua console. The other runtimes have nothing equivalent to open.
